messages:
alex: Heads-up: scheduled fan firmware update in eu-central next Tue 02:00-05:00 UTC. We’ll do per-rack staggered drains and soft reboots. Affected pools: gpu-eu-highmem, gpu-eu-standard. Expect ~10-15% token capacity drop in the region while the cohort is cycling. Please ack and flag any blockers.

maria: acked. can we run a small canary on one rack first? want to validate NVMe and BMC stability before full sweep. :white_check_mark:

derek: +1 on canary. also note netops flagged a flaky top-of-rack in az-eu-2 last week — suggest avoiding that rack for canary.

alex: good call. canary rack: eu-rack-07 (no TOC incidents). schedule below: canary 02:00-02:30, cooldown/monitor 02:30-03:00, then roll 03:00-05:00.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary job created: `maintenance/canary/4956789012-eu-fan-fw` (ETA 02:00). Will post status updates.

nina: what's the plan for tenant backfill? do we drain into burst pools or pause new scheduling? cost concern if we spin up cross-region backfill.

alex: prefer local backfill (soft-evict with migration) up to 20% of pool capacity. beyond that we'll fail-over to dedicated spare pools in us-west with strict egress limits. cost tradeoff estimated +$400 for the window if cross-region backfill used. open to suggestions.

maria: we should prioritize reserved/dedicated tenants to avoid SLA hits — add tagging rule to scheduler: `reserved_first=true` for the window.

alex: added scheduler policy `reserved_first=true` for maintenance window. also added `no_cross_region_backfill` flag for non-critical workloads.

derek: monitoring check list for canary and roll: CPU/GPU temp, fan speeds, BMC syslog, NIC errors, and p95 latency on hosted API routes. Runbook note: if BMC fails to come up after reboot, escalate to hardware team immediately and skip rack.

alex: runbook snippet pasted: ```
1) cordon nodes in rack
2) drain non-reserved pods with `--grace-period=120` and `--eviction-type=soft`
3) run firmware flash: `fwupdmgr update --device fanctrl --file fan_v2.1.bin`
4) reboot nodes in cohort
5) verify BMC/syslog + smbios for reboots
6) uncordon if healthy
```

ops-bot: maintenance/canary/4956789012-eu-fan-fw: success — canary completed, no regressions in 30m window.

nina: thanks. can we reduce the drain grace-period to 60s for gpu-eu-standard? those jobs are short and it'd cut the window by ~15m.

maria: I'm worried about stateful tasks. maybe do 60s only for ephemeral workloads (tag `ephemeral=true`). keep 120s for stateful.

alex: ok: updated job to use `--grace-period=60` for ephemeral workloads and keep 120 for others.

derek: one more ask — add a temporary autoscaler bump +10% of spare nodes in region for pre-warm (will reduce eviction pressure). cost impact ~+$120.

alex: agreed. schedule autoscaler bump from 01:30-05:30. ops-billing: note incremental spend ~+$520 including backfill contingency.

maria: comms: will send an external notice to affected customers with the planned window and expected degraded capacity. ping me draft and I'll add SLA language.

alex: will draft and post to #announcements by EOD today. thanks everyone.

ops-bot: maintenance/4956789012: completed at 04:52 UTC. final status: rolled 12 racks, 0 failed firmware flashes, 2 transient NIC errors resolved by retry, capacity dip peak 13%.
